mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0% and remains above this level for 3 months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that reduces corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for 3 months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate and declines in payrolls indicate labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or Rank IC for interaction term over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, rising consumer credit and housing starts signal strong household spending that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansion when RSAFS and HOUST are rising, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment over the past 6 months indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS has increased for 6 consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.2 percentage points in a single month, it signals economic weakness that reduces consumer confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production and high inflation indicate a supply shock that increases costs and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or Rank IC for interaction term over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During early recovery phases, rising industrial production signals improving manufacturing activity that boosts corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during early recovery when INDPRO is rising, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
